package.answer: This package pairs PE deal, valuation, and healthcare-market skills with practical AI decision-making and organizational strategy—an especially natural bridge from your healthcare consulting background. Prioritize the PE and healthcare finance foundations, then layer in AI strategy; the Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 options are expected courses based on this year’s offerings.

items.title: Introduction to Private Equity
items.why: Builds the broad practitioner-level foundation for evaluating healthcare PE opportunities and understanding how the asset class works.
items.evidence: a holistic view of the Private Equity business from a practitioner’s perspective

items.title: Private Equity: Leveraged Buyouts
items.why: Develops the LBO screening and diligence lens central to assessing buyout targets, including healthcare companies.
items.evidence: how private equity professionals evaluate opportunities and manage due diligence

items.title: Security Analysis & Valuation
items.why: Strengthens the fundamental valuation skills needed to judge a healthcare target’s investment case.
items.evidence: fundamental firm valuation is a primary part of the job

items.title: Private Equity: The Deal
items.why: Gives you hands-on practice evaluating an investment opportunity from the perspective of a PE investor.
items.evidence: puts students in the seat of the private equity investor evaluating a live investment opportunity

items.title: Mergers & Acquisitions
items.why: Adds transactional and numerical M&A fluency relevant to executing deals at a private equity firm.
items.evidence: expected within leading Wall Street investment banks and private equity firms

items.title: Healthcare Policy, Finance, and Economics
items.why: Builds healthcare-specific fluency in the financing and economic forces that shape targets and markets.
items.evidence: Economic and Financial drivers of the domestic healthcare system

items.title: Innovation, Investments, and New Frontiers in Medicine
items.why: Helps you assess life-sciences investment opportunities across pharma, devices, and diagnostics.
items.evidence: critical assessment of the life science industries

items.title: Health Care Strategy
items.why: Deepens your understanding of how healthcare-market incentives and competitive strategy affect profits and outcomes.
items.evidence: how strategic interactions among firms impact profits, health outcomes, and social welfare

items.title: Generative AI for Managers
items.why: Gives you a manager’s framework for evaluating and leading generative-AI integration in healthcare organizations.
items.evidence: understand, evaluate, and lead the integration of Generative AI solutions within organizations

items.title: AI for Business Decisions
items.why: Builds practical understanding of how predictive and generative AI can inform repeatable business decisions.
items.evidence: how organizations use predictive AI to make repeatable, data-informed decisions at scale

items.title: Empirical Strategy with AI
items.why: Adds hands-on practice applying AI-enabled quantitative methods to real business problems and strategic choices.
items.evidence: hands-on experience applying quantitative methods to real-world business problems

items.title: Analytics in the Age of AI
items.why: Sharpens your ability to structure ambiguous AI-era business decisions around objectives, constraints, and tradeoffs.

My pick this week: **AI cybersecurity is moving from a theoretical concern to an operational one.**

- The same week, the UK reportedly announced more than £600 million for AI security. I’d treat that figure cautiously: the source I found is a secondary report, not a government announcement. ([note.com, Oct 24](https://note.com/ripe_crab6964/n/ncdb36497faed?hl=en))
